_meta.description: Criteria for `/code-review --refactor` (#3797). Applied in place of the Step 5 charter criteria and the Step 5c domain questions. `wideScan: true` means a match triggers the all-files scan for other sites of the same pattern.

criteria.name: Duplication
criteria.lookFor: Blocks of logic, literals or structure repeated within the file or matching code elsewhere — copy-pasted functions, parallel switch/if ladders, repeated constant tables — that one shared definition could replace.

criteria.name: Extractable helper
criteria.lookFor: An inline sequence with a nameable purpose (parse, normalize, format, resolve a path, read-and-validate a file) that is, or is likely to be, written again elsewhere and would read better as one named helper.

criteria.name: Complexity
criteria.lookFor: Functions that are long, deeply nested or carry many branches or flags, where splitting, early returns or a lookup table would make the control flow easier to follow without changing behavior.

criteria.name: Naming
criteria.lookFor: Identifiers whose names mislead or say nothing about what they hold or do — abbreviations, stale names after a behavior change, one concept under several names — where a rename alone would clarify the code.

criteria.name: Dead code
criteria.lookFor: Unreachable branches, unused functions, exports, parameters, variables or imports, and commented-out code that nothing references and that can be removed without changing behavior.

criteria.name: Convention drift
criteria.lookFor: Code that departs from a pattern the rest of the codebase follows for the same job — a hand-rolled version of an existing shared helper, a different error-reporting shape, a different file-reading or argument-parsing idiom.
